reason: The check itself (a new Deno audit script in scripts/audit/) can be written offline, but the verify criterion — 'audit runs and produces a per-repo pass/fail table with evidence' — requires enumerating org repos and reading each repo's tag rulesets + bypass_actors via the GitHub API (`gh api repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets?targets=tag&includes_parents=true` and `/rulesets/{id}`). The sandbox has no GitHub credentials and api.github.com is blocked (returns 'GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session'); only `git clone` of public repos works, and repo enumeration is impossible without the API. Additionally, the enterprise-level refs/tags/* ruleset that trellis#34 describes is only fully readable (bypass actors) with org/enterprise-admin scope, the same posture scripts/audit.mjs already needs. So the code can be drafted here, but the org-wide findings table cannot be produced or proven in this sandbox.

plan: Read trellis#34 and mint#18/#19 to pin down what 'release identity' concretely is (a GitHub App slug, a bot user, or the human maintainer) and how a repo declares it — likely trellis.json / repo-config; if it is not declared anywhere yet, the check must fall back to 'any bypass_actor with bypass_mode always on the tag-creation rule' and report the actor list as evidence.

Create scripts/audit/release-tags.ts (Deno, modeled on scripts/audit/actions.ts): enumerate non-archived repos via `gh repo list bounded-systems --json name`; classify a repo as mint-released if .github/workflows/release.yml or publish-jsr.yml exists (via git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1) AND its `on.push.tags` matches `v*` (raw contents fetch); optionally also detect `mint` in deno.json tasks / trellis.json.

In the same script, for each mint-released repo fetch `repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets?targets=tag&includes_parents=true`, then each `/rulesets/{id}` (and `orgs/{o}/rulesets/{id}` for org-level); a ruleset with enforcement=active, a `creation` rule, and conditions.ref_name.include matching refs/tags/* (or ~ALL) is a tag-creation restriction; PASS iff some such ruleset has a bypass_actors entry (bypass_mode always) for the release identity, or no active restriction applies; FAIL otherwise, with evidence = workflow path + ruleset id/name/source (enterprise/org/repo) + bypass actor list.

Print a markdown per-repo table (repo | mint-released? | tag-creation restricted? | release-identity bypass? | verdict | evidence) and a Summary line; report-only by default (exit 0), `--strict` exits 1 on FAIL — mirroring actions.ts's phased promotion.
Add `audit:release-tags` and `audit:release-tags:strict` tasks to deno.json (needs --allow-run=gh --allow-env); keep fmt/lint include of scripts/audit/.

Add .github/workflows/release-tags-audit.yml (copy of actions-audit.yml: harden-runner, checkout persist-credentials:false, setup-deno v2.x, all SHA-pinned) — note that reading bypass_actors on org/enterprise rulesets may need the org-admin App token that audit.mjs uses rather than github.token; wire the same secret if so, and document the token posture in the workflow header.

risks: Sandbox cannot run the audit: no GitHub credentials, api.github.com blocked; the findings half of the task is unverifiable here and the verify criterion cannot be met without an org-admin token.

'Release identity' is not defined machine-readably anywhere in this repo; trellis#34 is still open, so the contract (who the release actor is, where it is declared) may not be settled — the check may have to encode a heuristic that later drifts from trellis's model.

The restricting ruleset is enterprise-level (per trellis#34); GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets?includes_parents=true lists it but the bypass_actors detail on an enterprise ruleset may not be readable even with org-admin scope, forcing an 'unknown' verdict rather than pass/fail.

GitHub ruleset API shape: bypass_actors have actor_type (Integration, OrganizationAdmin, RepositoryRole, Team, DeployKey) and actor_id; mapping that to 'the release identity' needs the App's installation id or a role, which is easy to get wrong.
Mint-released detection by filename (release.yml/publish-jsr.yml) will misclassify repos with differently-named tag-triggered workflows or hand-cut releases; false negatives hide real GH013 failures.
Rate limits: per-repo tree + N contents + rulesets fetches across ~72 repos with the concurrency pool of 10; fine with a token, but keep the pool bounded.

The `mint` repo itself shows no default-branch rules in CONFORMANCE.md, so the org's ruleset landscape is uneven; the check must handle repos with zero rulesets (treat as 'unrestricted → PASS' but flag).
Spell gate (cspell) will fail on new identifiers unless added to cspell.json words list.
